entities.name: PMID:25073001
observations: Primary study tested PD-1 pathway blockade after T-cell receptor stimulation in sarcoidosis cells.
Lymphocytes with reduced proliferative capacity showed increased proliferation after PD-1 pathway blockade.
Sarcoidosis had increased PD-1-positive CD4-positive T cells versus controls (P<0.0001); fewer PD-1-positive CD4 cells accompanied spontaneous clinical resolution, not progression.

entities.name: PMID:27564547
observations: Mechanistic follow-up confirmed increased PD-1-positive CD4-positive T cells and reduced proliferation in sarcoidosis versus controls (P<0.001).
PD-1 expression inversely correlated with proliferative capacity (r=-0.70, P<0.001).
After PD-1 pathway blockade, PI3K, AKT, mTOR-related gene and protein expression reverted toward healthy-control levels.

entities.name: Sarcoidosis
observations: In the cited studies, progressive sarcoidosis was associated with PD-1-positive CD4-positive T-cell accumulation and impaired T-cell receptor-stimulated proliferation.
The evidence concerns ex vivo human sarcoidosis cells and does not establish clinical efficacy of PD-1 blockade as a treatment.
